title: NASA Uniform Patches
slide_intent: Teach designers to make an agency and a person’s role readable on clothing. Position and contrast must work with garment construction and with other badges a wearer may carry.
strategic_value: NASA can distinguish general personnel from emergency or security teams while retaining agency identification across uniforms, protective clothing and headwear.
demonstration: Two patch specimens compare the general white patch with a red emergency or security patch and a separate dark service strip. Seven garment and equipment drawings show chest, shoulder, coat-back and helmet placements.
practical_value: Choose the patch by personnel role, then use the corresponding garment drawing to locate it. The lab coat and hardhat examples specify different sizes for their larger marks.

content_islands.name: Personnel and placement guidance
content_islands.spec: Set the title and explanatory columns along the top. Describe placement relative to a pocket and the special arrangement for emergency or security personnel.

content_islands.name: Patch specimens
content_islands.spec: Place both systems side by side at upper right. Keep the service strip visibly separate beneath the red installation patch.

content_islands.name: Garment applications
content_islands.spec: Arrange the flight jacket, shirt, flight suit, coat, blazer, emergency shirt and helmet in a single comparison field below the rule. Show each mark on the relevant visible surface.
